newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP resumes Ok Tedi copper shipments.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP resumes Ok Tedi copper shipments.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday it was resuming shipments of copper concentrates from its Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea following rains during the weekend.
"We've got one barge up there and four more going up now," a BHP spokesman told Reuters from Port Moresby.
The spokesman said rains, starting on Friday, had caused water levels on the Fly River to rise sufficiently to allow barges to be transported from the port of Kiunga down river to the Gulf of Papua.
The journey takes about two days, he said. Each barge holds about 25,000 tonnes of copper concentrates, bound mainly for Asia and Europe.
At maximum shipping, eight vessels navigate the river at one time, he said.
River traffic was first suspended on June 2, but the spokesman said it was impossible to say how long it would remain open given the unpredictability of the weather.
"We can't say that things will be going back to normal yet," he said.
The port of Kiunga currently has about 140,000 tonnes of cocentrate which is transported to the port by pipeline from the mine in PNG's Western province.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters. BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
